artworks.title: Thersites Accosts Achilles
artworks.description: Selous' Victorian illustration for Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida: the deformed railer Thersites confronts Achilles — the Iliad's insolent voice from the ranks reinvented as the play's bitter fool.

artworks.title: Odysseus Beats Thersites (Iliad Book II, Pope edition)
artworks.description: Plate from an illustrated Pope Iliad: in the assembly of Book II, Odysseus strikes Thersites with Agamemnon's sceptre — the epic's rare punishment of a common soldier for mocking kings.

artworks.title: Achilles Strikes Thersites (Roman sarcophagus relief)
artworks.description: Detail of a sarcophagus in the Antalya Museum: Achilles kills Thersites for mocking his grief over Penthesilea — the Cyclic sequel to the Iliad, carved in marble for a Roman tomb.

popCulture.title: Thersites
popCulture.description: The Iliad's ugly railer — beaten by Odysseus for mocking kings — remains the name for insolent speech in the ranks.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: Book II's assembly scene keeps Thersites as the epic's rare voice from below the heroes' circle.
